t2.thesis: BETA is a cash-rich, pre-revenue eVTOL name with positive FAA newsflow into the print, but its last two beats were sold, so I sit only slightly above the base rate.
reasons: Cluster base rate for drones/space/defense is above average at 0.586, and BMO timing is mildly favorable.
The last two prints were EPS beats (+18% and +46%) yet both fell at the exit-A open, which suggests the market sells beats on cash burn and opex growth.
The EPS estimate was cut about 21% over 90 days, which lowers the bar, though the estimate rests on only 2 analysts.
Pre-print FAA milestones (Special Airworthiness Certificate, eIPP flights) are already public, which limits the upside surprise from operations news.
Options lean bullish (call IV above put IV, put/call volume 0.30), but the ~17% implied move signals a near coin-flip with large tails.
t2.deciding_variable: Whether FY2026 revenue guidance ($42-50M) is held or raised and whether the Adjusted EBITDA burn guide (-$400 to -$445M) widens, alongside certification timeline updates for CX300 and A250.

t2.moved_from_prior: Down about 3 points, from 0.57 to 0.54. Two consecutive negative reactions to beats, the stock 47% off its 52-week high and down 10% in a month, and heavy opex and capex growth outweigh the lowered EPS bar and bullish option skew.

theses.wrong_if: The burn guide widens or certification timelines slip
